messages:
alex: Heads-up — follow-up from the slashed-latency RFC. Quick summary: we want a lightweight hedging protocol that issues a speculative call to a smaller/quantized model when the primary model's tail latency threatens SLOs. Not an always-on hedge — only trigger based on telemetry & adaptive thresholds. RFC link: https://go/rfcs/slashed-latency-hedge

maya: sounds useful. main worry is quality regressions and signal noise — how do we avoid masking regressions (e.g., hedge returns a subtly different completion and the app silently prefers it)? :thinking:

ryan: Router/runtime boundary question: who decides to hedge? options: 1) Router-level (fast decision, can check p99 telemetry, throttle hedges per-tenant) 2) Runtime-level (runtime observes kernel-level stall and issues speculative peer call) 3) Hybrid (router flags candidate -> runtime executes). I prefer Router-level for observability and quota control. We need a small API contract: router adds header `x-hedge-mode: speculative` and `x-hedge-budget: 0.15` and runtime accepts/ignores.

sam: cost perspective — hedging multiplies token cost for hedged requests. we need a hard cap per-tenant and global rate limit. Also differentiate sync hedges (issue both and take first) vs async (race and fallback). sync is simpler but expensive.

toni: telemetry proposal (minimal set): `inference.latency.p95`, `inference.latency.p99`, `hedge.invocations`, `hedge.win_rate` (percentage of requests where hedge finished first), `eval.quality.delta` (periodic A/B eval on sampled prompts). We'll gate rollout on both latency improvement and quality delta. Example thresholds: require p99 improvement > 20ms and quality delta <= 1.5% loss on sampled evals.

ryan: here's a config sketch for router feature flags (proto):
```yaml
hedge_policy:
  enabled: true
  trigger_window_ms: 250    # only attempt hedges when observed tail > this
  hedge_budget: 0.1         # fraction of QPS eligible for hedging per-tenant
  fallback_models: ["redwood-mini-7b-q4", "redwood-2b-q4"]
  mode: sync                # sync | async | staged
  max_extra_qps: 0.2        # cap extra load from hedges
```

maya: config looks good. important to include a sampling mode that records full pairs (primary vs hedge) to the eval pipeline (prompt_id mapping) so we can run offline diff checks & synthetic evals.

sam: rollout plan suggestion: canary at 0.5% users for 6h -> 2% for 12h -> 10% stable. Abort if: `hedge.invocations / total_requests > 0.35` OR `eval.quality.delta > 3%` OR `inference.latency.p99` regression. Keep cost alert: `billing.hedge_tokens > $X/day`.

alex: interface note: router must attach a correlation id for paired requests (x-hedge-cid) so downstream logs/eval can join traces. Also must expose a proxy metric `hedge.applied_by_tenant` for per-tenant debugging.

deploy-bot: deploy started: hedge-controller v2 -> canary-arch (1%) by ops-deploy (triggered by alex). status: queued

ryan: edge case: models with nondeterministic generation might return different but equally-valid outputs. evaluation pipeline should include semantic similarity (embedding distance) + task-specific checks, not just token-diff. Propose `eval.thresholds` per model family.

toni: defense-in-depth: fallback circuit-breaker per-tenant if hedged responses cause repeated user-level errors (e.g., hallucination rate spikes). Expose a runtime flag `hedge_circuit_trips` that disables hedging for N minutes.

sam: will need billing semantics: mark tokens from hedges as `hedge_token` in billing exports so finance can analyze.

maya: ops question: how to handle function-calling / tool calls? we can't race tool side-effects. For stateful tool calls we must not issue speculative external side-effecting calls. so hedging should be disabled for requests with `x-tool-call: true` or enter a safe mode that hedges only model-only completions.

alex: good catch. add rule: hedging disabled when `tools` or `function_call` present OR when request flagged `side_effect_sensitive=true`.

ryan: implementation phasing: 1) router-only passive mode (sampling + metrics, no hedges) 2) pilot sync-hedging for read-only text gen 3) build quota & billing hooks 4) add runtime hybrid optimizations (fast-kick speculative from runtime when kernel stalls).

alex: action items:
- ryan: PR for router header contract + config schema (https://go/changes/hedge-router-contract)
- maya: add sampling hooks to eval infra + prompt mapping (https://go/boards/hedge-eval)
- sam: cost/billing tags and budget alert (ticket created)
- toni: define metric thresholds & create dashboard (dash id: D-HEdge-001)
- ops: monitor canary from deploy-bot and hold on abort criteria

alex: final: let's keep this thread as the single source for clarifying the interface. schedule 30m sync tomorrow if anyone wants to walk through the config. :thumbsup:
